# Kendrick Chia’s Post

1mo

Most people immediately recoil when they hear this: “Buy residential property under a Pte Ltd.” And honestly… the reaction is understandable. With 65% ABSD imposed by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore, the obvious disadvantage is brutal and upfront. It kills most discussions before they even begin. But here’s the interesting part. If we move past the tax headline and look at structure instead of sticker shock, there are some surprising strategic advantages. 1. Ring-fenced liability Holding property under a company separates personal and corporate risk. For entrepreneurs or professionals exposed to litigation risk, this containment can matter more than people think. 2. Clean equity structuring A Pte Ltd allows flexible shareholding arrangements. You can allocate equity, dividends, and control rights in ways that are harder to do when co-owning as individuals. This becomes relevant in joint ventures, blended families, or succession planning. 3. Earnings retention mechanics Rental income sits within the company. Instead of flowing to personal income tax brackets immediately, profits can be retained, reinvested, or deployed into other corporate assets. 4. Exit optionality at the share level In certain situations, you may transfer shares of the company rather than the property itself. Structurally, that can open doors for strategic exits, partnerships, or capital raising. 5. Portfolio architecture discipline When property sits inside a corporate vehicle, it forces you to think in balance sheet terms: debt ratios, retained earnings, return on equity. It becomes an asset in a portfolio strategy, not an emotional purchase. Now, let’s be clear. For most individual investors in Singapore, the 65% ABSD makes this route economically inefficient. The math often overwhelms the structure. But strategy is not just about what is popular. It’s about understanding the full toolbox, then choosing the right instrument for your stage of capital growth. Sometimes the biggest advantage is not in using a structure. It’s in knowing exactly when not to.

The succession piece in point 2 is probably the one most people miss. Once shareholding gets flexible, the question stops being about the asset and starts being about who controls it and when.

#sturbucks#turnaround story business restructuring is not only about cost cutting and investing in technology, but also about the more human and subtle nuances such as client experience, that plays a huge part, often neglected in such processes.

 

 

Leysan Gilfanova, CPA 

 3w 

 

Starbucks cycled through 4 CEOs in less than 3 years. September 2024: Brian Niccol takes over. His job: fix the $30B mess Narasimhan left in 17 months. So what happened there? March 2023: Laxman Narasimhan becomes CEO. On paper, he looked perfect. 19 years at McKinsey. PepsiCo executive across 100+ countries. Just turned around Reckitt (saved £2B, grew 8.6%). The board gave him 6 months to train as a barista. He relocated from London to Seattle. He was all in. His plan? "Triple Shot Reinvention With Two Pumps." Yes, that was the actual name. $600M in technology. Supply chain optimization. Data-driven decisions. It looked smart. It sounded strategic. But he brought the wrong playbook. At Reckitt, success came from cost cutting and portfolio optimization. At Starbucks, success comes from customer experience and baristas who know your name. And he never asked customers why they stopped coming. Mobile orders hit 31%. The coffeehouse where people loved to hangout for hours became a pickup counter they rushed through. Sales dropped for the first time in 3 years. Then traffic down 6%. Then stock down 20%. $30B in market value — gone. August 13, 2024. Before market open. Board announces Narasimhan out. Effective immediately. No transition. Just out. Stock soars 24% that day. Biggest single-day gain in years. $20B in value created by his departure. Brian Niccol's plan? "Back to Starbucks." Back to the coffeehouse. Back to customer experience. Not more data. Not more technology. Customer experience. He spent 6 years turning around Chipotle after food safety scandals. Stock up 773%. Margins from 17% to 26%. But Chipotle took 3 years to turn around and Starbucks is 10x bigger: 41,000 stores across 80+ countries. That's the CFO lesson: You can spend $600M on technology and optimize every part of supply chain — but the wrong playbook costs billions. No amount of data replaces listening to your customers. 18 months in, customers are coming back: U.S. visits up for the first time in 8 quarters. Global store sales up 4%. Brian Niccol's turnaround seems to be working — but is 18 months enough to declare victory? ♻️ If this was useful, share it. 🔔 I'm Leysan, CFO who breaks down billion-dollar business models and makes it simple. Tesco just made the barcode obsolete. 2D barcodes are replacing 1D barcodes across their shelves, and the pilot is already live across 12 product lines. Lemons, limes, steaks and sausages among them. But the Tesco trial is just the start. Across the broader 2D barcode ecosystem, the implications for brands go well beyond the shelf: 1. Real-time expiry visibility, so you're not relying on static print dates that don't account for actual storage conditions 2. Direct consumer engagement at the moment of purchase, turning a barcode scan into a branded touchpoint 3. Richer first-party data on how and when customers are interacting with your products post-purchase 4. Faster recall response, because if something goes wrong, you know exactly where a product is in the supply chain Starting with a handful of SKUs is exactly the kind of measured entry point that makes a technology shift feel manageable. And the 2027 deadline from GS1 means this isn't a "wait and see" situation for much longer. If you're mapping out what this transition looks like for your catalogue, happy to walk you through it.

MS Awareness Month is personal for me. My mother lived with multiple sclerosis for many years, and I saw firsthand how this disease can slowly take away independence, mobility, and too often, much more. Her experience is one of the reasons I dedicated my career to advancing MS research. Today, the science is moving faster than ever. Researchers around the world are developing better treatments, identifying earlier signals of disease, and working toward something that once felt impossible: preventing MS before it starts. But scientific progress doesn’t happen on its own. It moves forward because people choose to support it. This MS Awareness Month, I’m asking our community to help accelerate the research that will change the trajectory of this disease. If MS has touched your life, or the life of someone you care about, I hope you’ll consider supporting the work that is bringing us closer to a world free of MS. # Hironao Okahana’s Post

Some reflections around a new brief my team at the American Council on Education released last week, "Reengaging stopped-out learners: Institutional strategies for return and completion." - The “flexible program delivery” is a requisite for removing barriers against reengagement of stopped-out learners. Learners will not return to the same structure that “failed” them the first time. - Even if learners “stopped out” in the eyes of IHEs, but their learning may continue to take place outside of the traditional academy – whether at workplace or home. Structurally and culturally, we need a system that more widely recognizes these learning as a part of postsecondary learning. - With increasing prevalence of short-term certificates, more students may “stop-out” in a traditional sense. In addition to designing postsecondary learning for those who can commit to four years at the age of 18, we also need to design a process that “stop-out” is the feature (e.g., stack-ability of short-term credentials toward a degree). Excellent work by Julia Napier and Danielle Melidona, conducting the study, and also leading a very lively discussion at the sideline of the ACEx. Special thanks to our colleagues at Pearson for their partnership and support for this project. Much to be done, let's keep at it. https://lnkd.in/eWfHedHk

Aske is right to sound the alarm here... but I want to add some nuance. The talent gap he's describing isn't just a volume problem — it's a type problem. NPSP and Agentforce for Nonprofits aren't on the same skill continuum. NPSP was a managed package installed on top of Salesforce. The entire discipline of "being good at NPSP" was built around working within and around that package — knowing its boundaries, managing its upgrade cycles, understanding what you could and couldn't touch. That's genuinely hard-won expertise. But AFNP is a core product. The rules didn't just change — they inverted. Some of those package instincts are active liabilities now. The question isn't only "how many NPC implementations have you done." It's "do you understand why best practices are fundamentally different — and have you let go of the right ones?" There's another layer worth naming honestly. Many of the best people in the nonprofit Salesforce ecosystem came up as accidental admins — self-taught, deeply specialized, shaped almost entirely by the NPSP world. That origin story produced brilliant practitioners. It also means a significant part of the community has never had to think about long-term core product stewardship, or worked in development paradigms outside the NPSP continuum. That's not a character flaw. It's just the reality of how the community grew. It matters now. Here's what I think we sometimes miss: there's a ready, experienced talent pool that's largely being overlooked. Industries Cloud practitioners — people who know Financial Services Cloud, Public Sector Solutions, Health Cloud — already understand AFNP's architecture deeply, because so much of it shares DNA with products they've mastered for years. YES, they need to learn nonprofit language, culture, and operations. That's real. But they already know how to make the product sing. At BrightHelm Partners, when NPC first launched, we made a deliberate choice: go learn the sister products. Not because we thought them superior, but because the documentation for then-NPC didn't exist yet and we had enough humility to recognize that Industries Cloud practitioners had been building in this paradigm longer than we had. They had things to teach us. The real opportunity here isn't waiting for the nonprofit community's AFNP experience to accumulate. It's cross-pollination. Bohle will be showcasing three examples of its pharmaceutical processing technology for the manufacture of oral solid doses at INTERPHEX 2026 in New York City: the QbCon® 1 continuous granulation and drying system, the BFC 5 laboratory tablet coater, and the BTS 200 pharmaceutical sieving machine.

QbCon® 1 Continuous Wet Granulation and Drying System. Image Credit: L.B. Bohle Maschinen und Verfahren GmbH

Visitors to the L.B. Bohle stand at Booth 1619 will see how the company’s latest equipment supports continuous manufacturing and improves pharmaceutical production processes and product development efficiency.

These three technology highlights will demonstrate advances in continuous oral solid dose manufacturing, laboratory tablet coating, and pharmaceutical particle processing.

## QbCon® 1 Truly Continuous Wet Granulation and Drying

The QbCon® 1 Continuous Wet Granulation and Drying System represents a significant advancement in continuous oral solid dose production. The system combines continuous raw material dosing, twin-screw wet granulation and drying in one compact, mobile unit.

Advanced features include sophisticated material conveyance, very short residence times in the dryer, automatic exhaust filter self-cleaning and high containment. Integrated control systems increase operational flexibility while enhancing operator safety.

The QbCon® 1 is designed to deliver narrow residence-time distributions that simplify material traceability in continuous processes. This makes it easier to track materials from raw ingredients to finished tablets, while supporting accelerated scale-up.

Integrated process analytics also help to reduce resource consumption and shorten pharmaceutical development times.

Building Scouting America Troop 161, a BSA Scout Troop for youth with intellectual and developmental disabilities. This past fall I met with D161's superintendent and Board of Education, and secured their partnership to become the Chartered Organization for our new Troop. After that I gathered a large handful of Scout Leaders, who have either been my mentors, or I have worked with as a leader in another unit. All who have proven their dedication to the Scouting movement, and their support of inclusion of Scouts with disabilities. Then as a group we built a Troop with six awesome Scouts, with equally awesome parents. Last night was our first Red and Green Celebration, and I was sworn in as the first Scoutmaster of Troop 161. L’œuvre de Kate Van Doren ne part pas d’une question esthétique, mais d’une fonction : la guérison. À partir de ce point précis, sa pratique se déplace hors du champ de la déconstruction qui caractérise une large part de l’art contemporain pour s’inscrire dans un dispositif réparateur, où l’expérience n’est pas interrogée mais réorganisée.

Chez Van Doren, l’art ne produit pas de crise. Il absorbe. Là où certaines démarches contemporaines cherchent à fragmenter les récits, à perturber les codes de représentation ou à exposer les structures invisibles du pouvoir, son travail opère dans une logique inverse. Il rassemble, il apaise, il reformule. Il ne s’agit pas de rompre, mais de rétablir une continuité.

Son projet central, Healing Words Project, constitue l’architecture la plus explicite de cette orientation. Fondé sur la participation de milliers de femmes et de voix marginalisées, il met en place un protocole de traduction presque clinique. Le vécu devient langage, le langage s’inscrit sur le corps, le corps est photographié, puis transposé en peinture. Une chaîne linéaire se déploie du trauma vers le mot, puis du mot vers l’image.

Cette linéarité fait la force du projet autant qu’elle en révèle la limite. Elle garantit une lisibilité immédiate et une accessibilité émotionnelle qui permet au spectateur d’entrer sans résistance. Mais elle élimine, dans le même geste, toute opacité. Or, c’est souvent dans l’opacité que se loge la pensée critique.

Van Doren ne cherche pas à produire de la résistance. Elle cherche à contenir la fracture.

Sur le plan esthétique, son travail s’inscrit dans une forme de réalisme empathique maîtrisé avec rigueur. Les visages sont construits avec précision, les textures contrôlées, la lumière stabilisée. Cette virtuosité technique, indéniable, reste néanmoins subordonnée à une fonction narrative. Il s’agit de rendre visible la vulnérabilité et de donner une forme lisible à la résilience.

Le corps, dans ce dispositif, n’est pas problématisé. Il est utilisé. Surface d’inscription plus que champ de tension, il accueille les mots sans que son statut soit interrogé. Les phrases qui le traversent ne fragmentent pas sa représentation, elles la renforcent. Le corps devient support, non enjeu.

# Katja Schuurman onthult: 'Ik heb OCD, dwanggedachten, ADHD, borderline en ook nog de overgang'

9 apr 2026, 21:23

Link gekopieerd

Katja Schuurman is in een nieuwe aflevering van de podcast Borrelpraat eerlijk over haar psychische gezondheid en hoe die haar relaties beïnvloedt. De actrice vertelt dat bij haar meerdere diagnoses zijn vastgesteld en dat ze daar in haar liefdesleven altijd open over is.

"Ik heb OCD, dwanggedachten, maar daar heb ik goede medicijnen voor, ADHD, borderline en ook nog de overgang. Nou, gefeliciteerd!", zegt Katja, geciteerd door weekblad Weekend. Toch beschouwt ze zichzelf niet als een slachtoffer. Integendeel: "Ik zie mezelf gewoon als een topsporter, want ik pareer het lekker."

Medicatie is voor haar een belangrijk onderdeel hiervan. Katja geeft aan dat ze Duloxetine gebruikt en vindt dat er veel meer openheid over dit soort middelen mag komen. Volgens haar heerst er nog steeds onnodig veel schaamte rondom het gebruik van medicatie, terwijl het juist kan ondersteunen wanneer de chemische balans in je hersenen verstoord is.

Ook in haar liefdesleven wil ze daar duidelijk en open over zijn. Wanneer haar wordt gevraagd hoe ze haar mentale gezondheid en een relatie combineert, reageert ze met een knipoog en gevoel voor humor. "Ik ben op dit moment drie jaar vrijgezel. Ik ben twee keer gescheiden, dus daar heb je je antwoord."

Volgens Katja komt haar ADHD ook tot uiting in alledaagse, kleine dingen. Zo laat ze regelmatig iets uit haar handen vallen of stoot ze per ongeluk dingen om. Ze merkt dat niet iedereen daar even makkelijk mee omgaat. "Ik pleur ook de hele tijd dingen om", vertelt Katja lachend. Tegen partners is ze daar vooraf duidelijk over. "Ik zei: ‘Dit gaat heel vaak gebeuren, dus please: als je van mij houdt, lach erom. Maar ga je niet lopen storen, want ik doe het niet expres. Ik ruim het zelf op.’"

De Vandaag Inside-tafel en Chris Woerts reageerden eerder op een onthulling van Katja Schuurman in De Klassenavond. Bekijk het terug in de video bovenaan deze pagina!

Last week's Memorandum of Understanding(MoU) between Proxima Fusion, Freistaat Bayern, RWE, and the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics(IPP) is a turning point for fusion in Europe. This marks the moment European fusion moves into industrial reality, with Proxima at the center of that shift. Like everyone in fusion, I came into the field to see it entering this new phase, and it’s spectacular to see it happen now.

The MoU is more than a partnership announcement. It is, in the words of RWE CEO Dr. Markus Krebber, "a cornerstone for future energy supply in Bavaria, Germany, and Europe." For the first time, world-class fusion science, capital, infrastructure, and political commitment are aligned behind a single project – going from demonstrator to commercial fusion power plant, in Europe.

Bavarian Minister-President Dr. Markus Söder perfectly captured the scale of what this coalition represents: "This is a completely new chapter in German energy policy, and for the whole world."

I couldn't agree more. For me, it’s also a moment of pride, seeing our public institutions coming together and recognizing that Europe needs to step up together with its private sector.

## The Funding Architecture That Makes It Real

Bold ambitions require bold investment. MP Söder announced at the press conference that Bavaria is committing €400 million in state funding towards the Alpha project. This commitment is key to unlocking something equally important: German federal support. Under Germany's High-Tech Agenda, national funding follows demonstrated state-level commitment. More than €2.4B of public investment is already committed for the next three years by the German government in its Fusion Action Plan.

In the MoU, the four partners agreed on a joint project proposal. Söder made the goal clear: "We hope the federal government will also contribute, so that together we can reach over one billion euros for a major national project." Proxima will also step up to contribute €400M of private investment toward Alpha, which is estimated to cost €2B in total

By committing first, Bavaria de-risks federal participation for the Alpha project and creates the conditions for private capital to follow. This is how large-scale industrial projects get built.

Founded in 2021 by the Swedish and German giants, Cellcentric focuses on developing, producing, and commercializing hydrogen fuel cell systems for heavy-duty trucks and sustainable transportation, with operations in Germany and Canada. This move marks a significant shift in the hydrogen landscape. By joining Volvo and Daimler as an equal partner, Toyota—a pioneer in hydrogen technology—is set to accelerate the commercialization of fuel cells as a key technology for decarbonizing long-haul transport. The partnership allows the companies to combine Toyota’s deep knowledge with existing expertise, bringing significant commercial opportunities and sharing the substantial R&D costs associated with hydrogen technology. "Welcoming Toyota onboard will be a big leap towards realising decarbonisation of our industries," said Martin Lundstedt, President and CEO of Volvo Group. Following the closing of the transaction, Toyota intends to contribute its complementary technical know-how to the joint venture, solidifying cellcentric's position as a global leader in fuel cell systems. The initiative highlights the critical role of hydrogen as a long-term solution alongside battery-electric alternatives in the automotive industry's green transition. Jörg Schlagbauer

Viele Kolleginnen und Kollegen aus der Wechselschicht wissen im Moment nicht, wie sie zuverlässig nach Hause kommen sollen – denn die 22:17‑Uhr‑Verbindung am Audi Bahnhalt fällt seit Wochen ersatzlos aus. Die Alternativen sind für Schichtbeschäftigte kaum nutzbar: Zu früh, zu spät, oder ohne funktionierenden Ersatzverkehr. Für viele bedeutet die Situation zusätzlich zum Arbeitsalltag Stress, Unsicherheit und unnötig lange Wartezeiten – gerade am späten Abend und bei winterlichen Temperaturen. Deshalb habe ich mich bereits vor über zwei Wochen schriftlich an die Deutsche Bahn gewandt und auf eine schnelle Lösung gedrängt. Da bis heute weder eine Rückmeldung eingegangen ist noch eine Verbesserung erkennbar war, war es mir wichtig, auch persönlich vor Ort zu sein. Diese Woche habe ich daher am Audi Bahnhalt direkt mit Kolleginnen und Kollegen gesprochen und mir ihre Erfahrungen schildern lassen. Diese Gespräche haben mich sehr bewegt – denn sie zeigen deutlich, wie sehr eine fehlende oder unzuverlässige Anbindung den Alltag vieler Menschen beeinflusst. Gemeinsam mit einem Vertreter der Unternehmensseite sowie Pressevertretern wollten wir deshalb ein klares Zeichen setzen: Diese Situation braucht Aufmerksamkeit – und sie braucht eine Lösung. Mobilität ist für Beschäftigte im Schichtbetrieb kein Randthema, sondern Grundvoraussetzung dafür, Arbeit und Privatleben vereinbaren zu können. Als Betriebsratsvorsitzender ist es mir ein zentrales Anliegen, solche Herausforderungen frühzeitig aufzugreifen, sichtbar zu machen und für Verbesserungen zu werben. Ich hoffe sehr, dass wir hier zeitnah Fortschritte sehen – im Sinne all jener, die täglich auf verlässliche Verbindungen angewiesen sind.#AUDIAG#AudiBahnhalt#AudiBetriebsrat

Over the last few years, I have been reflecting on a fundamental shift happening across industrial operations. Most plants are still operating in a reactive or time-based maintenance model—despite significant investments in automation and digital systems. The real opportunity lies in moving beyond monitoring… towards insight-driven and value-led operations. After nearly 13 years, three distinct Alphabet organizations, and countless lessons learned, my time at Google is coming to a close today. When I reflect on this journey, I'm most proud of the rare opportunity I had to build and scale systems across all three of Alphabet’s main functions (G&A, Tech, and GBO): - G&A (Google People Services): Scaling HR operations and systems to support a workforce that grew from 35,000 to nearly 200,000. - Tech (Google Fiber): Helping design, build, and scale the fiber optic networks that brought high-speed internet to communities like Edgehill and North Nashville. - GBO (Google Cloud / Google Public Sector): Delivering cloud technology, conversational AI, and Augmented Reality Microscopes to our public sector partners. Of the many lessons I’m taking with me, three core principles stand out: - Build for scale: If a task only needs doing once, get it done. But if it needs to be done twice, build a system to do it a googol times. - High expectations require great enablement: Expecting greatness from a team must be paired with equipping them with the right tools. When you combine an audacious goal with true enablement, you get moonshots. - Communication is a choice: Clarity is a prerequisite for execution. Whether writing a project charter or an email, every word matters. Write the document, cut the fluff, and leave out the parts people skip. I am incredibly grateful to the brilliant colleagues, mentors, and friends who made this chapter so rewarding. To everyone I’ve worked with: thank you, be well, do good, and keep in touch. And next week: I am thrilled to announce that I will be joining the incredible team at Databricks!

Hoping your next job isn’t so stressful it makes you lose all your hair 😉

I’ve had a bunch of chats this week with senior leaders across a variety of industries. Two clear themes related to AI emerge very quickly: 1. Everyone feels behind. This is universal, no matter where you and your company may be on the adoption curve. The pressure to meet this particular moment is very real. 2. Super users who’ve deeply incorporated AI into their workflows are having trouble unplugging. (Doubly so if they’re just getting access to Claude CoWork). The ability to create and hold healthy boundaries with work is blurring right now. I’ll just share my own approach to these in case it’s helpful to anyone else. My mantra is increasingly “forget what you do, remember who you are.” The velocity of work made possible by these tools is addictive…it feels like the cost of “doing” is near zero. When I step back and center on my values, the frantic pressure recedes a bit. It’s easier to find natural stopping points, and I think my outputs are stronger across the board (work, family, life).

# Beitrag von Katja Herrmann

- Diesen Beitrag melden

** Die wichtigste Frage für Vermögensschutz stellt fast niemand..... ** Internationale Vermögensdiversifikation gilt schon lange als Königsweg. Immobilien in Dubai. Grundstück/Häuser in Nordzypern. Apartments in Spanien oder Portugal. Auslandskonten. Die Idee dahinter: Vermögen global verteilen – Risiken reduzieren. Doch die aktuellen Krisen zeigen eine unbequeme Wahrheit: Internationale Diversifikation schützt nicht automatisch. Denn am Ende bleibt eine entscheidende Frage: Kannst Du Dein Vermögen im Ernstfall überhaupt bewegen? Immobilien sind wertvoll. Aber sie bleiben stehen. Und jeder hier weiß, dass Gold, Immobilien und Aktien die Assets sind, die in jedem gut strukturierten Portfolio die Hauptrolle spielen. Aber eines können sie alle nicht: Im Krisenfall mit Dir den Raum verlassen. Leise. Unauffällig. Fast schwerelos. Genau deshalb rückt ein Thema immer stärker in den Fokus vermögender Anleger: Mobiles Vermögen. Physische Sachwerte mit hoher Wertdichte. International anerkannt. Systemunabhängige, eigene Verwahrung ohne Fremdrisiken. Nicht als Ersatz für andere Anlagen. Sondern als zusätzlicher mobiler Baustein. Denn Vermögensschutz bedeutet nicht nur zu streuen. Sondern auch zu überlegen - und das zeigen gerade wieder die aktuellen Ereignisse: Was bleibt beweglich, wenn alles andere stehen bleibt oder nicht auf Zugriff ist? 👉 Ein Einfamilienhaus in der Hosentasche - das geht mit Diamanten. 💬 Frage an Euch: Auf welche mobilen Vermögenswerte setzt Du bereits? Wie mobil ist Dein Vermögen wirklich?#Vermögensschutz#Sachwerte#PortfolioStrategie#Diversifikation#Diamanten
